evidence: app/src/routes/abilities/[name].js:1-79 — entire feature is one self-contained route file; deleting the directory removes the pages
app/src/document.js:20-23 — nav is centralized and contains no ability links, so no nav edit needed
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js:342-351 — cross-links to /abilities live in the Pokémon page's Abilities section and must be edited separately
app/src/lib/api.js:141-143 — getAbility becomes dead code after removal
app/src/lib/components.js:23,38 — the `hidden` card option and document.css:209 `.hidden-ability` styles exist only for the abilities page
removability.rationale: Routes are self-contained and the nav is centralized, but a cross-linked feature still touches the Pokémon page and leaves three small dead-code pockets (api helper, card option, CSS) that only a grep would find.

evidence: app/src/lib/components.js:30 — every card's sprite comes from spriteUrl(species.id) in pokemonCard; one fix covers home, moves, abilities and types lists
app/src/lib/api.js:226-243 — uniqueSpeciesFromPokemonReferences is the single normalizer behind all three secondary card lists
app/src/routes/moves/[name].js:83-84 — the count-line + pokemonCardList section is duplicated verbatim in abilities/[name].js:73-74 and types/[name].js:112-113
app/src/routes/[name].js — not-found template block duplicated in moves:58-62, abilities:56-60, types/[name]:82-86, pokemon:285-289
changeability.rationale: The sprite/list bug fixes land in one obvious seam shared by every card list, which is the important case; page-level changes (sorting, error copy, not-found UI) have to be repeated across three or four near-identical templates.

evidence: app/src/routes/moves/[name].js:29-45 — handler normalizes raw API records into a plain view-model before the template; templates never touch API shapes
app/src/routes/(home).client.js:32 — client script contracts the server only via the #home-results element id and same-origin HTML fetch; no API or state leakage
app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.js:36 — sort contract is limited to stable selectors and data-* attributes emitted by the server template
app/src/lib/api.js:64-105 — transport/caching and display helpers (humanize, dexNumber, typeClassName) share one grab-bag module
app/src/routes/(home).js:15 and app/package.json:7 — the GRACILE_BUILD env convention is an implicit contract spanning package.json plus all six route files
coupling.rationale: Server/client separation and data normalization are genuinely clean, and components depend on a tiny species shape; the deductions are implicit magic-ID contracts, an undifferentiated lib/api.js, and a build-mode env var agreed across seven files.

evidence: app/src/lib/components.js:22-38 — pokemonCard captures real variation with two narrow options (showTypes, hidden) instead of flag creep; good stretch
app/src/lib/api.js:111-127 — getSpeciesIndex is reusable by any new resource page (an /items section would reuse it, getRecord, englishName, displayValue)
app/src/routes/moves/[name].js:18 — BUILDING() guard copy-pasted at (home).js:15, pokemon/[name].js:23, abilities/[name].js:15, types/index.js:7, types/[name].js:13
app/src/lib/api.js:27,222 — dead exports getApiBase and sortSpeciesById
app/src/features — empty placeholder directory; app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].js:103 hardcodes `type-${row.typeName}` instead of typeClassName (api.js:100)
abstraction_design.rationale: The component and data-helper layers stretch to similar cases without copying, but the route layer is boilerplate-by-duplication: every new resource page re-copies the guard, try/catch-404 and not-found template, and there are several small dead-code artifacts.

findings.issue: The not-found template, the try/catch → { notFound: true } handler shape and the BUILDING() guard are duplicated in all five content routes (moves, abilities, types/[name], pokemon/[name], plus guards in (home).js and types/index.js); a new resource page must copy all three.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared `notFoundTemplate(context)` (or a `withNotFound(handler)` wrapper) and a single `isBuild()` helper into src/lib/, and use them from every route.

findings.issue: The 'count-line + pokemonCardList' section is copy-pasted in moves, abilities/[name].js:73-74 and types/[name].js:112-113, so any list-wide behaviour (sorting, pagination, empty state) must be implemented three or four times.
findings.suggestion: Add a `pokemonListSection(pokemon, { heading, showTypes })` component in lib/components.js that renders the count line, the list and any shared list controls.

findings.issue: The GRACILE_BUILD=1 build-mode convention is an implicit contract: it is read in six separate route files (e.g. app/src/routes/(home).js:15), so changing build-time behaviour means seven edits, and a route that forgets the guard silently fails during build.
findings.suggestion: Centralise in one lib helper (or drop the guard entirely with output: 'server' if handlers aren't invoked at build time) and import it from each route.

findings.issue: lib/api.js mixes HTTP transport, caching and URL building (lines 1-63, 245-247) with display helpers (humanize, englishName, dexNumber, typeClassName, displayValue) in one 247-line grab-bag that every route imports from.
findings.suggestion: Split into lib/pokeapi.js (transport + caching) and lib/display.js (humanize/dexNumber/etc.) so the display rules can change without touching the fetch layer.

findings.issue: Dead code: sortSpeciesById (api.js:222) and getApiBase (api.js:27) are exported but never imported; app/src/features/ is an empty placeholder directory.
findings.suggestion: Delete the unused exports and the empty directory, or wire sortSpeciesById into the card lists where it was evidently intended.

findings.issue: Sprite/artwork derivation is split: cards always build the URL by pattern via spriteUrl (components.js:30), while the detail page picks pokemon.sprites with a spriteUrl(pokemon.id) fallback, so a sprite-policy change (e.g. null sprites for unshipped sets) has two sites.
findings.suggestion: Route all sprite selection through one helper (e.g. cardSprite(pokemon) and artwork(pokemon)) in lib/api.js or components.js.

findings.issue: The move table inlines `type-${row.typeName}`, duplicating the typeClassName helper (api.js:100-102) also bypassed by types/index.js:40.
findings.suggestion: Use typeClassName(row.typeName) in both templates so a class-naming change stays in one place.

findings.issue: The home route and its client script are coupled by an undocumented magic id `home-results` ((home).client.js:32 replaces that element); renaming it in the template silently breaks live filtering.
findings.suggestion: Define the id as a shared constant (exported from lib or a comment at both sites) or use a data attribute documented in both files.

summary: A idiomatic, current-stable Gracile 0.11 app (Express adapter matches the official starter, per-route client scripts, handler→props→template flow) whose data and card-rendering layers are well factored: sprite and species normalization each have a single seam covering every card list. The weaknesses are route-level boilerplate — not-found handling, the build guard and the count-line section are copy-pasted in every route — plus a grab-bag lib/api.js and a few dead exports. Most changes land in one to three files; the classic ones (card fixes, API/caching changes) land in exactly one.
